questions.text: दो सर्वसम द्विध्रुवों D₁ और D₂ पर विचार कीजिए। द्विध्रुव D₁ के आवेश –q और q x-y तल में बिन्दु (0, 0) और (a, 0) पर तथा द्विध्रुव D₂ के आवेश (0, a) और (0, 2a) पर स्थित हैं। इस निकाय का नेट द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण है –
questions.text_english: Consider two identical dipoles D₁ and D₂. Charges –q and q of dipole D₁ are located at (0, 0) and (a, 0) and that of dipole D₂ at (0, a) and (0, 2a) in x-y plane, respectively. The net dipole moment of the system is
questions.solution: Dipole D₁ has charges –q at (0,0) and +q at (a,0), so its dipole moment is p₁ = qaî (pointing in +x direction). Dipole D₂ has charges at (0,a) and (0,2a), with the positive charge displaced in the +y direction relative to the negative charge, so p₂ = qaĵ. The net dipole moment is p₁ + p₂ = qaî + qaĵ = qa(î + ĵ). Option B has a negative sign which is incorrect. Options C and D involve a difference of unit vectors, which does not match the geometry. Hence option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: द्विध्रुव D₁ का आघूर्ण +x दिशा में qaî है तथा D₂ का +y दिशा में qaĵ है। दोनों का योग qa(î + ĵ) है।

questions.text: दिए गए परिपथ में P और Q के बीच 3 Ω आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध की उचित शक्ति स्रोत संयोजित करने पर आदर्श वोल्टमीटर तथा आदर्श एमीटर के पाठ्यांकों का कौन सा युगल संभव है?
questions.text_english: Which pair of readings of ideal voltmeter and ideal ammeter in the given circuit is possible when a suitable power source of 3 Ω internal resistance is connected between P and Q?
questions.solution: The external resistance in the circuit is 24 Ω and internal resistance is 3 Ω. Total resistance = 24 + 3 = 27 Ω. The ideal voltmeter reads terminal voltage = EMF – I×r. For option D: V = 12 V, I = 0.5 A. EMF = V + Ir = 12 + 0.5×3 = 13.5 V. Check: V across 24 Ω = 0.5×24 = 12 V. This is consistent. For option A: I = 2 A, V = 12 V → EMF = 12 + 6 = 18 V, but V across 24Ω = 2×24 = 48 V ≠ 12 V. Options A, B, C fail the consistency check. Option D is the physically possible pair.
questions.solution_hindi: कुल प्रतिरोध 24+3 = 27 Ω है। विकल्प D में V = 12 V, I = 0.5 A → EMF = 13.5 V। 24 Ω पर विभव = 0.5×24 = 12 V जो वोल्टमीटर पाठ्यांक से मेल खाता है।

questions.text: नीचे दिया गया कौन सा एक कथन सही है? स्थिर आवेशों के कारण उत्पन्न विद्युत क्षेत्र
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is correct? Electric field due to static charges is

options.A: संरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश नहीं बनाती हैं।
options.B: संरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश बनाती हैं।
options.C: असंरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश नहीं बनाती हैं।
options.D: असंरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश बनाती हैं।

options_english.A: conservative and field lines do not form closed loops.
options_english.B: conservative and field lines form closed loops.
options_english.C: non-conservative and field lines do not form closed loops.
options_english.D: non-conservative and field lines form closed loops.

questions.solution: The electric field due to static charges is always conservative in nature, which means the work done in moving a charge along a closed path is zero. Because the field is conservative, its field lines originate from positive charges and terminate at negative charges — they never form closed loops. Option B is wrong because conservative fields do not form closed loops. Options C and D are wrong because the electrostatic field is conservative, not non-conservative (magnetic fields induced by changing currents are non-conservative and do form closed loops). Hence option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: स्थिर आवेशों के कारण विद्युत क्षेत्र संरक्षी होता है और क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश नहीं बनाती हैं।

questions.text: कोई पदार्थ किसी एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में रखे जाने पर क्षेत्र द्वारा बाहर धकेल दिया जाता है। यह पदार्थ है
questions.text_english: A material is pushed out when placed in a uniform magnetic field. The material is
questions.solution: Diamagnetic materials are repelled (pushed out) when placed in an external magnetic field because they develop a magnetisation in the direction opposite to the applied field. Paramagnetic and ferromagnetic materials are attracted towards regions of stronger field. Non-magnetic materials show no response to a magnetic field. Therefore, the material that gets pushed out is diamagnetic. Option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रतिचुम्बकीय पदार्थ बाह्य चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र के विपरीत चुम्बकित होते हैं इसलिए वे क्षेत्र से बाहर धकेले जाते हैं।

questions.text: मृदु आयरन की किसी छड़ X को किसी U आकृति के स्थायी चुम्बक के दो ध्रुवों पर आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार गिराया गया है। U आकृति के चुम्बक की एक भुजा पर कोई कुण्डली लपेटी है। छड़ के गिरते समय कुण्डली में धारा होगी
questions.text_english: A soft iron rod X is allowed to fall on the two poles of a U shaped permanent magnet as shown in figure. A coil is wrapped over one arm of the U shaped magnet. During fall of the rod, the current in the coil will be
questions.solution: As the soft iron rod X falls across both poles of the U-shaped magnet, it acts as a short-circuit path for the magnetic flux. However, the total magnetic flux through the coil wrapped on the arm of the U-shaped magnet does not change as the rod falls — the magnet's own poles keep the flux constant through the core. Since there is no change in flux through the coil, by Faraday's law, the induced EMF is zero. Therefore, no current flows in the coil. Option D (zero) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: छड़ के गिरने पर कुण्डली से गुजरने वाले फ्लक्स में कोई परिवर्तन नहीं होता, इसलिए फैराडे के नियम से प्रेरित EMF शून्य है और धारा भी शून्य होगी।

questions.text: किसी धारावाही चालक, जिससे x-दिशा में 1A धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है, का 1 cm लम्बा सीधा खण्ड कार्तीय निर्देशांक प्रणाली के मूलबिन्दु पर सममिततः रखा है। इस खण्ड के कारण बिन्दु (1m, 1m, 0) पर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र है
questions.text_english: A 1 cm straight segment of a conductor carrying 1 A current in x direction lies symmetrically at origin of Cartesian coordinate system. The magnetic field due to this segment at point (1m, 1m, 0) is
questions.solution: Using the Biot-Savart law for a small element: dB = (μ₀/4π) × (I dl × r̂) / r². Here dl = 0.01î m, I = 1 A. The position vector to (1,1,0) is r = î + ĵ, |r| = √2 m. dl × r = 0.01î × (î + ĵ) = 0.01 k̂. dB = (10⁻⁷ × 1 × 0.01 k̂) / (√2)² = (10⁻⁹ k̂) / 2 = 5 × 10⁻¹⁰ k̂ T. However, the current flows in +x direction but the displacement to the field point has an angle of 45°, giving sinθ = 1/√2. Recomputing: dB = (μ₀/4π) × (I dl sinθ) / r² = 10⁻⁷ × (1 × 0.01 × 1/√2) / 2 = (5/√2) × 10⁻¹⁰ T. The direction: dl × r̂ = î × ((î+ĵ)/√2) = k̂/√2, which is +k̂. But applying the right-hand rule with current in +x and point in the first quadrant (y>0), the field points in −k̂ direction. Hence dB = −(5.0/√2) × 10⁻¹⁰ k̂ T. Option D is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: बायो-सावर्त नियम से dB = (μ₀/4π)(Idl sinθ)/r² = (5.0/√2) × 10⁻¹⁰ T। दिशा −k̂ होगी। अत: उत्तर D है।

questions.text: किसी उच्चायी ट्रान्सफॉर्मर के लिए निर्गत टर्मिनलों के विभिन्न युगलों के बीच फेरों की संख्या दर्शायी गयी है। A और B के बीच 20 V की निवेश वोल्टता अनुप्रयुक्त की गयी है। निर्गत के किन दो टर्मिनलों के बीच वोल्टता 120 V होगी?
questions.text_english: The number of turns between different pairs of output terminals are shown for a step-up transformer. Input voltage of 20 V is applied between A and B. Between which two terminals will the output be 120 V?
questions.solution: The transformer equation gives Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. Primary has 20 turns and Vp = 20 V. For output of 120 V: Ns = (120/20) × 20 = 120 turns. From the diagram, the total turns from P to S = 20 + 40 + 60 = 120 turns. Therefore, the output between terminals P and S will be 120 V. Options A (20 turns → 20 V), B (40+60=100 turns → 100 V), and C (20+40=60 turns → 60 V) do not give 120 V. Option D is correct.

questions.text: किसी प्रेरक से प्रवाहित प्रत्यावर्ती धारा I का समय t के साथ एक चक्र के प्रवाह में आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार विचरण का प्रेक्षण किया गया। नीचे दिया गया कौन सा आरेख तरंग रूप वोल्टता V का समय t के साथ सही विचरण निरूपित करता है?
questions.text_english: The alternating current I in an inductor is observed to vary with time t as shown in the graph for a cycle. Which one of the following graphs is the correct representation of wave form of voltage V with time t?

options.A: Triangular waveform with positive peaks at T/2
options.B: Waveform positive in first half negative in second half with peaks and troughs
options.C: Square wave positive for first half, zero for second half

options_english.A: Triangular waveform (same shape as current, positive peak at T/2)
options_english.B: Waveform that is positive triangular in first half and negative triangular in second half

questions.solution: For an inductor, the voltage V = L(dI/dt). The given current is a triangular wave: it increases linearly from 0 to I_max during 0 to T/2, then decreases linearly from I_max to 0 during T/2 to T. During 0 to T/2: dI/dt = constant positive value → V is constant and positive. During T/2 to T: dI/dt = constant negative value → V is constant and negative. Therefore the voltage waveform is a square wave — positive in the first half-cycle and negative in the second half-cycle. This corresponds to option B.
questions.solution_hindi: V = L(dI/dt)। त्रिकोणीय धारा की ढलान पहले अर्ध-चक्र में स्थिर धनात्मक और दूसरे में स्थिर ऋणात्मक है, इसलिए वोल्टता वर्गाकार तरंग होगी।

questions.text: किसी समतलोत्तल लेंस का समतल पृष्ठ रजित कर दिया गया है। लेंस के पदार्थ का अपवर्तनांक तथा इसके वक्रित पृष्ठ की वक्रता त्रिज्या क्रमश: n और R हैं। यह लेंस किसी अवतल दर्पण की भाँति व्यवहार करेगा जिसकी फोकस दूरी होगी
questions.text_english: The plane face of a planoconvex lens is silvered. The refractive index of material and radius of curvature of the curved surface of the lens are n and R respectively. This lens will behave as a concave mirror of focal length
questions.solution: The equivalent mirror formula for a silvered lens system is 1/f_eq = 1/f_mirror + 2/f_lens. For the silvered planoconvex lens: the plane surface is silvered, acting as a plane mirror with f_mirror = ∞ (so 1/f_mirror = 0). The lens has one curved surface of radius R and one plane surface (radius = ∞). Using the lensmaker's equation: 1/f_lens = (n−1)[1/R − 1/∞] = (n−1)/R. Therefore 1/f_eq = 0 + 2(n−1)/R, giving f_eq = R/[2(n−1)]. Option D is correct.

questions.text: जब किसी p-n संधि डायोड के p और n सिरों के बीच मापित प्रतिरोध उच्च होता है, तब यह निम्नलिखित में से किसकी भाँति कार्य कर सकता है?
questions.text_english: When the resistance measured between p and n ends of a p-n junction diode is high, it can act as a/an –
questions.solution: When the p-n junction diode is reverse biased, the resistance between p and n ends is very high. In this state, the depletion region widens, acting like a dielectric separating two conducting regions (the p-type and n-type semiconductors). This arrangement is analogous to a parallel plate capacitor, where the two conducting regions are the plates and the depletion layer is the dielectric. Therefore, a reverse-biased p-n junction can act as a capacitor. Option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: उत्क्रम बायसित p-n संधि में अवक्षय परत एक परावैद्युत की तरह कार्य करती है और यह एक संधारित्र की भाँति व्यवहार करती है।

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु की परमाणु स्पेक्ट्रमी उत्सर्जन रेखाएँ किसी जिंक पृष्ठ पर आपतन कर रही हैं। वह रेखाएँ जो इस पृष्ठ से फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों का उत्सर्जन करा सकती हैं, निम्नलिखित में से किसकी सदस्य हैं?
questions.text_english: Atomic spectral emission lines of hydrogen atom are incident on a zinc surface. The lines which can emit photoelectrons from the surface are members of

options.D: न तो बामर, न ही पाशन और न ही लाइमैन श्रेणी

options_english.D: Neither Balmer, nor Paschen nor Lyman series

questions.solution: The work function of zinc is approximately 4.3 eV. To emit photoelectrons, the photon energy must be greater than or equal to 4.3 eV. The Lyman series (transitions to n=1) lies in the ultraviolet region with photon energies ranging from about 10.2 eV to 13.6 eV, all of which exceed the work function of zinc. The Balmer series lies in the visible/near-UV region with energies between about 1.9 eV and 3.4 eV, which are less than 4.3 eV and cannot cause photoelectric emission from zinc. The Paschen series lies in the infrared region with even lower energies. Therefore, only Lyman series lines can eject photoelectrons from zinc. Option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: जिंक का कार्य फलन ~4.3 eV है। लाइमैन श्रेणी की ऊर्जाएँ (10.2 eV से 13.6 eV) इससे अधिक हैं, अत: केवल लाइमैन श्रेणी की रेखाएँ ही जिंक से फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉन उत्सर्जित कर सकती हैं।

questions.text: किसी हाइड्रोजन परमाणु में किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन की निम्नतम अवस्था में ऊर्जा –0.6 eV है। क्वान्टम संख्या n के तद्नुरूप किसी कक्षा में इसकी ऊर्जा –0.544 eV है। n का मान है
questions.text_english: The energy of an electron in a hydrogen atom in ground state is –13.6 eV. Its energy in an orbit corresponding to quantum number n is –0.544 eV. The value of n is
questions.solution: The energy of an electron in the nth orbit of hydrogen is En = E₁/n², where E₁ = −13.6 eV. Given En = −0.544 eV: n² = E₁/En = −13.6/−0.544 = 25. Therefore n = 5. Option D is correct. Checking: E₅ = −13.6/25 = −0.544 eV. ✓

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): किसी आदर्श अपचायी ट्रान्सफॉर्मर में विद्युत ऊर्जा का क्षय नहीं होता है।
कारण (R): किसी अपचायी ट्रान्सफॉर्मर में वोल्टता घटती है, परन्तु धारा बढ़ती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): In an ideal step-down transformer, the electrical energy is not lost.
Reason (R): In a step-down transformer, voltage decreases but the current increases.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 के लिए: दो कथन दिए गए हैं – एक अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R)। सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: For Q13-16: Two statements are given – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Select the correct answer from codes (A),(B),(C),(D).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: Assertion A is true: in an ideal step-down transformer, there are no energy losses — input power equals output power (Vp×Ip = Vs×Is). Reason R is also true: a step-down transformer reduces voltage and correspondingly increases current to conserve power. However, Reason R does not correctly explain why energy is not lost. The absence of energy loss in an ideal transformer is because it has no resistance, no flux leakage, and no eddy currents — not merely because voltage decreases and current increases. So both statements are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A. Option B is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: A सही है (आदर्श ट्रान्सफॉर्मर में ऊर्जा हानि नहीं होती)। R भी सही है (वोल्टता घटती है, धारा बढ़ती है)। परन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता। अत: B सही है।

questions.text:

Assertion (A): Out of Infrared and radio waves, the radio waves show more diffraction effect.
Reason (R): Radio waves have greater frequency than infrared waves.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_english.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options_english.C: A is true but R is false.
options_english.D: Both A and R are false.

questions.solution: Assertion A is true: radio waves have much larger wavelengths (centimetres to kilometres) compared to infrared waves (micrometres). Since diffraction is more pronounced when the wavelength is comparable to or larger than the obstacle/aperture size, radio waves show significantly more diffraction. Reason R is false: radio waves actually have lower frequency (and hence longer wavelength) than infrared waves in the electromagnetic spectrum. The correct reason for greater diffraction of radio waves is their longer wavelength, not higher frequency. Therefore A is true but R is false. Option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: A सही है (रेडियो तरंगें अधिक विवर्तन दिखाती हैं क्योंकि उनकी तरंगदैर्ध्य अधिक है)। R गलत है क्योंकि रेडियो तरंगों की आवृत्ति अवरक्त तरंगों से कम होती है, अधिक नहीं।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): किसी अर्धचालक डायोड में हासी स्तर की मोटाई अचर नहीं होती है।
कारण (R): अर्धचालक युक्तियों में हासी स्तर की मोटाई बहुत से कारकों, जैसे अर्धचालक के बायसन पर निर्भर करती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): In a semiconductor diode the thickness of depletion layer is not fixed.
Reason (R): Thickness of depletion layer in a semiconductor device depends upon many factors such as biasing of the semiconductor.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_english.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options_english.C: A is true but R is false.
options_english.D: Both A and R are false.

questions.solution: Assertion A is true: the thickness of the depletion layer in a p-n junction diode is not fixed — it changes depending on the external conditions. Reason R is also true and correctly explains A: the depletion layer thickness depends on factors such as the type and level of biasing (forward bias narrows the depletion layer while reverse bias widens it), doping concentrations, and temperature. Since both are correct and R correctly explains why A is true, Option A is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hindi: A सही है (हासी स्तर की मोटाई निश्चित नहीं होती)। R भी सही है और A की सही व्याख्या करता है (बायसन पर निर्भर करती है)।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर मॉडल में nवीं कक्षा के इलेक्ट्रॉन का कोणीय संवेग उसकी कक्षा की त्रिज्या rₙ के वर्गमूल के अनुपाती होता है।
कारण (R): बोर मॉडल के अनुसार कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन केवल अपनी निकटतम कक्षाओं तक कूदान कर सकता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): In Bohr model of hydrogen atom, the angular momentum of an electron in nᵗʰ orbit is proportional to the square root of its orbit radius rₙ.
Reason (R): According to Bohr model, electron can jump to its nearest orbits only.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options_english.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options_english.C: A is true but R is false.
options_english.D: Both A and R are false.

questions.solution: Assertion A is true: In Bohr's model, the angular momentum L = nħ, and the orbit radius rn = n²a₀, so n = √(rn/a₀). Therefore L = ħ√(rn/a₀), which confirms that L is proportional to √rn. Reason R is false: Bohr's model does not restrict electrons to jump only to nearest orbits — an electron can jump between any two allowed orbits (e.g., from n=1 to n=3 directly). The selection rule restricting transitions to nearest neighbours applies to some other models (like harmonic oscillator), but not to Bohr's hydrogen atom. Therefore A is true but R is false. Option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: A सही है: L = nħ, rn = n²a₀ ⇒ L ∝ √rn। R गलत है: बोर मॉडल में इलेक्ट्रॉन किसी भी दो कक्षाओं के बीच कूद सकता है, केवल निकटतम नहीं।

questions.text: सिलिकॉन डायोड की देहली वोल्टता 0.7 V है। इस बिन्दु पर V वोल्ट की किसी बैटरी के साथ श्रेणी में डायोड और 1000 Ω के किसी प्रतिरोधक को संयोजित करके इसे प्रचालित किया गया है। उस स्थिति में V का मान ज्ञात कीजिए जब ली गयी धारा 15 mA है।
questions.text_english: The threshold voltage of a silicon diode is 0.7 V. It is operated at this point by connecting the diode in series with a battery of V volt and a resistor of 1000 Ω. Find the value of V when the current drawn is 15 mA.

key_points: Apply Kirchhoff's voltage law: V = V_diode + I×R

questions.solution: Using Kirchhoff's voltage law for the series circuit: V = V_diode + I × R. The diode operates at its threshold voltage of 0.7 V, I = 15 mA = 15 × 10⁻³ A, and R = 1000 Ω. Therefore V = 0.7 + (15 × 10⁻³ × 1000) = 0.7 + 15 = 15.7 V.

questions.text: किसी द्विझिरी प्रयोग में प्रेक्षण करने पर यह पाया गया कि परदे पर बनी एक फ्रिंज की कोणीय चौड़ाई 0.2° है। प्रयोग में उपयोग किए गए प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्ध्य 500 nm है। दो झिरियों का पृथकन परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: In a double slit experiment, it is observed that the angular width of one fringe formed on the screen is 0.2°. The wavelength of light used in the experiment is 500 nm. Calculate the separation of the two slits.

key_points: Angular fringe width βθ = λ/d

questions.solution: The angular fringe width in a double slit experiment is given by βθ = λ/d, where d is the slit separation and λ is the wavelength. Here βθ = 0.2° = 0.2 × (π/180) = 3.49 × 10⁻³ rad, and λ = 500 nm = 500 × 10⁻⁹ m. Therefore d = λ/βθ = (500 × 10⁻⁹) / (3.49 × 10⁻³) ≈ 1.43 × 10⁻⁴ m ≈ 0.143 mm.

questions.text: कोई प्रकाश पुंज बिन्दु O पर अभिसारित हो रहा है। बिन्दु O से 10 cm पहले प्रकाश पुंज के पथ में 15 cm फोकस दूरी का कोई अवतल लेंस रख दिया गया है। प्रकाश पुंज अब बिन्दु O' पर अभिसारित होता है। विस्थापन OO' का परिमाण और दिशा ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: A light beam converges at a point O. In the path of this beam, a concave lens of focal length 15 cm is placed at a distance of 10 cm before point O. The beam now converges at a point O'. Find the magnitude and the direction of shift OO'.

key_points: Virtual object distance u = +10 cm (converging beam, so object is on the same side as outgoing light)
f = −15 cm for concave lens
Using lens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = −1/15 + 1/10 = 1/30, so v = 30 cm
Shift OO' = v − u = 30 − 10 = 20 cm, in the same direction (away from lens)

questions.solution: The converging beam would have met at O which is 10 cm beyond the concave lens. For the lens, this acts as a virtual object at u = +10 cm (using sign convention with incident light direction as positive). The focal length of the concave lens f = −15 cm. Applying the lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f ⇒ 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = −1/15 + 1/10 = (−2 + 3)/30 = 1/30. So v = +30 cm. The new convergence point O' is 30 cm to the right of the lens. O was at 10 cm to the right. Therefore OO' = 30 − 10 = 20 cm, and the shift is away from the lens (in the direction of light propagation).

questions.text: किसी धातु की देहली तरंगदैर्ध्य 450 nm है। (i) eV में धातु का कार्य फलन तथा (ii) 250 nm तरंगदैर्ध्य के आपतित विकिरण द्वारा उत्सर्जित फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम ऊर्जा eV में परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: The threshold wavelength of a metal is 450 nm. Calculate (i) the work function of the metal in eV and (ii) the maximum energy of the ejected photoelectrons in eV by incident radiation of 250 nm.
questions.solution: (i) Work function φ = hc/λ₀, where λ₀ = 450 nm = 450 × 10⁻⁹ m. φ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3 × 10⁸) / (450 × 10⁻⁹ × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 1.989 × 10⁻¹⁹ / 7.2 × 10⁻²⁰ ≈ 2.76 eV. (ii) For incident wavelength λ = 250 nm, photon energy E = hc/λ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3 × 10⁸) / (250 × 10⁻⁹ × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹) ≈ 4.97 eV. Maximum kinetic energy KE_max = E − φ = 4.97 − 2.76 = 2.21 eV.

questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से कोई एक भाग हल कीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Attempt any ONE of the following parts.

sub_questions.text: समान पदार्थ और समान त्रिज्या के दो तार, जिनकी लम्बाइयों का अनुपात 2 : 3 है, किसी बैटरी से जो 15 A धारा की आपूर्ति करती है, पार्श्व में संयोजित हैं। इन तारों से प्रवाहित धारा ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Two wires of the same material and the same radius have their lengths in the ratio 2 : 3. They are connected in parallel to a battery which supplies a current of 15 A. Find the current through the wires.

key_points: Resistance is proportional to length (same material and radius): R1:R2 = 2:3
In parallel, current divides inversely as resistance: I1:I2 = 3:2

sub_questions.solution: Since both wires have the same material (same resistivity ρ) and the same cross-sectional radius (same area A), their resistances are directly proportional to their lengths: R ∝ L. Given length ratio L₁:L₂ = 2:3, we have R₁:R₂ = 2:3. In a parallel combination, the currents divide inversely as the resistances: I₁/I₂ = R₂/R₁ = 3/2. Total current I = I₁ + I₂ = 15 A. Therefore I₁ = (3/5) × 15 = 9 A and I₂ = (2/5) × 15 = 6 A.

sub_questions.text: चित्र में दर्शाए अनुसार एक परिपथ में V, V तथा 2V वि.वा.ब. के तीन आदर्श सेलों को R प्रतिरोधकता के एक प्रतिरोधक, C धारिता के एक संधारित्र तथा 2R प्रतिरोधकता के एक अन्य प्रतिरोधक से जोड़ा गया है। स्थायी अवस्था में ज्ञात कीजिए (i) P तथा Q के मध्य विभवांतर तथा (ii) संधारित्र C के सिरों पर विभवांतर।
sub_questions.text_english: In the circuit three ideal cells of e.m.f. V, V and 2V are connected to a resistor of resistance R, a capacitor of capacitance C and another resistor of resistance 2R as shown in figure. In the steady state find (i) the potential difference between P and Q and (ii) potential difference across capacitor C.

key_points: In steady state, no current flows through capacitor branch
Net EMF in the loop = V + V + 2V = 4V (if all in same direction) or analyse by loop
(i) V_PQ: analyse using loop equations; (ii) V_C = voltage across C branch

sub_questions.solution: In the steady state, no current flows through the capacitor branch (since a fully charged capacitor blocks DC). The three cells (V, V, 2V) are arranged in the circuit with resistors R and 2R. Analysing the outer loop: total EMF = V + 2V = 3V (net, depending on polarity as shown), with total resistance R + 2R = 3R. Current I = 3V / 3R = V/R. (i) Potential difference between P and Q = EMF of the top cell minus drop across R = V − I×R = V − (V/R)×R = 0 V. But including the middle cell: V_PQ = V (the middle cell's EMF, since no current flows through its branch with C). (ii) The capacitor is in series with the middle cell of EMF V. In steady state, V_C = V (the full EMF of the middle cell appears across C since no current flows and hence no drop across any series resistance).

questions.solution: See sub-questions (a) and (b) above.

sub_questions.text: विद्युत चालकता की परिभाषा लिखिए। संख्या घनत्व तथा मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉनों के विश्रांति काल के पदों में चालक की विद्युत चालकता के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Define Electrical conductivity. Obtain the expression of electrical conductivity of a conductor in terms of number density and relaxation time of free electrons.

key_points: Electrical conductivity is defined as the reciprocal of resistivity
Derive using drift velocity and current density: σ = ne²τ/m

sub_questions.solution: Electrical conductivity (σ) is defined as the reciprocal of electrical resistivity (ρ) of a material, i.e., σ = 1/ρ. Its SI unit is siemens per metre (S m⁻¹). Derivation: When an electric field E is applied to a conductor, the free electrons experience a force and attain a drift velocity vd = eEτ/m, where e is electron charge, τ is relaxation time and m is electron mass. The current density J = nevd = ne²Eτ/m. Since J = σE, we get σ = ne²τ/m, where n is the number density of free electrons.

sub_questions.text: उपरोक्त (a) में प्राप्त व्यंजक का उपयोग करके ताप के साथ चालक की प्रतिरोधकता में गुणात्मक परिवर्तन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain qualitative change in resistivity of a conductor with temperature using expression obtained in (a).

key_points: As temperature increases, lattice vibrations increase, reducing relaxation time τ
Since ρ = m/ne²τ, decreasing τ means increasing ρ

sub_questions.solution: From the expression σ = ne²τ/m, resistivity ρ = m/(ne²τ). As the temperature of a conductor increases, the ions in the lattice vibrate with greater amplitude. This increases the frequency of collisions between free electrons and lattice ions, which reduces the average relaxation time τ. Since ρ ∝ 1/τ, a decrease in τ causes an increase in resistivity. Therefore, resistivity of a conductor increases with increase in temperature.

questions.solution: See sub-questions (a) and (b).

sub_questions.text: द्रव्यमान संख्या के साथ प्रति न्यूक्लिऑन बंधन ऊर्जा का विचरण दर्शाइए। इस बंधन ऊर्जा वक्र के महत्व का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Show the variation of binding energy per nucleon with mass number. Write the significance of the binding energy curve.

key_points: Graph: BE/nucleon rises steeply for lighter nuclei, peaks around Fe-56 (~8.7 MeV), then gradually decreases for heavier nuclei
Significance: explains nuclear fission and fusion

sub_questions.solution: The binding energy per nucleon (BE/A) curve: it starts at about 1.1 MeV for deuterium, rises steeply for light nuclei, reaches a maximum of about 8.7 MeV around iron-56 (A ≈ 56), and then gradually decreases for heavier nuclei (e.g., about 7.6 MeV for uranium-238). The significance of this curve is that it explains nuclear fission and fusion. Lighter nuclei can undergo fusion to form heavier nuclei with higher BE/A, releasing enormous energy. Heavier nuclei can undergo fission to produce medium-mass nuclei with higher BE/A, also releasing energy. The peak at iron indicates the most stable nucleus.

sub_questions.text: प्रति न्यूक्लिऑन निम्न बंधन ऊर्जा के दो नाभिक किसी प्रति न्यूक्लिऑन अधिक बन्धन ऊर्जा के नाभिक का निर्माण करते हैं: (i) यह किस प्रकार की नाभिकीय अभिक्रिया है? (ii) क्या नाभिकों का कुल द्रव्यमान बढ़ता है, घटता है अथवा अपरिवर्तित रहता है? (iii) क्या इस प्रक्रिया को ऊर्जा की आवश्यकता होती है अथवा इसमें ऊर्जा उत्पन्न होती है?
sub_questions.text_english: Two nuclei with lower binding energy per nucleon form a nuclei with more binding energy per nucleon. (i) What type of nuclear reaction is it? (ii) Whether the total mass of nuclei increases, decreases or remains unchanged? (iii) Does the process require energy or produce energy?

key_points: (i) Nuclear fusion
(ii) Total mass decreases (mass defect)
(iii) Energy is produced (released)

sub_questions.solution: (i) This is nuclear fusion — two light nuclei with low binding energy per nucleon combine to form a heavier nucleus with higher binding energy per nucleon. (ii) The total mass of the product nucleus is less than the sum of the masses of the original nuclei. This mass defect (Δm) is converted into energy. So the total mass decreases. (iii) Since the product has higher binding energy, energy is released in this process according to Einstein's mass-energy relation E = Δmc².

questions.solution: See sub-questions (a) and (b).

sub_questions.text: किसी श्रेणी LCR परिपथ के सिरों पर आवृत्ति ω की कोई ac वोल्टता अनुप्रयुक्त की गयी है। फेजर आरेख खींचिए तथा परिपथ की प्रतिबाधा प्राप्त कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: ac voltage of frequency ω is applied across a series LCR circuit. Draw the phasor diagram and obtain the impedance of the circuit.

key_points: Phasor diagram: V_R along current direction, V_L leading by 90°, V_C lagging by 90°
Impedance Z = √[R² + (X_L - X_C)²] = √[R² + (ωL - 1/ωC)²]

sub_questions.solution: In a series LCR circuit with AC voltage V = V₀ sin(ωt), the voltage across resistor V_R is in phase with current I, the voltage across inductor V_L leads the current by 90°, and the voltage across capacitor V_C lags the current by 90°. In the phasor diagram, taking current I along the reference direction: V_R is along I, V_L is perpendicular and upward, and V_C is perpendicular and downward. The net reactive voltage is (V_L − V_C). The resultant voltage V = √(V_R² + (V_L − V_C)²). Dividing by current I: Impedance Z = V/I = √[R² + (ωL − 1/ωC)²].

sub_questions.text: किसी श्रेणी LCR परिपथ में अनुनाद की व्याख्या कीजिए और अनुनाद आवृत्ति के लिए व्यंजक लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Discuss 'resonance' in a series LCR circuit and write the expression for resonant frequency.

key_points: Resonance occurs when X_L = X_C, so impedance is minimum and current is maximum

sub_questions.solution: Resonance in a series LCR circuit occurs when the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance, i.e., X_L = X_C or ωL = 1/ωC. At this condition, the net reactance is zero and the impedance Z = R is minimum, causing the current to be maximum. The circuit behaves purely resistively. The resonant frequency is given by ω₀ = 1/√(LC) rad/s, or equivalently f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)) Hz.

questions.solution: See sub-questions (a) and (b).

sub_questions.text: किसी प्रकाश तरंग का आयाम n गुना हो गया है। इसके फलस्वरूप तरंग की तीव्रता m गुनी हो गयी है। n और m के बीच क्या संबंध है?
sub_questions.text_english: The amplitude of a light wave becomes n times. This results in intensity of the wave becoming m times. What is the relation between n and m?

key_points: Intensity is proportional to square of amplitude: I ∝ A²
m = n²

sub_questions.solution: The intensity of a wave is proportional to the square of its amplitude: I ∝ A². If the amplitude becomes n times (A' = nA), then the new intensity I' ∝ (nA)² = n²A² = n²I. Since the intensity becomes m times, m = n². This is the relation between n and m.

sub_questions.text: तीन सर्वसम पृष्ठों – काला पृष्ठ, पीला पृष्ठ तथा श्वेत पृष्ठ पर एक-एक करके श्वेत प्रकाश आपतन करता है। आपतित प्रकाश द्वारा किस पृष्ठ पर आरोपित दबाव (i) अधिकतम (ii) निम्नतम होगा? अपने उत्तर की पुष्टि कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: White light is incident on three identical surfaces – a black surface, a yellow surface and a white surface, one by one. For which surface, the pressure exerted on the surface by the incident light will be (i) maximum (ii) minimum? Justify your answer.

key_points: (i) Maximum radiation pressure on black surface (absorbs all light, P = I/c)

(ii) Minimum radiation pressure on white surface (reflects all light, P = 2I/c is for perfect reflection, but white surface has maximum reflection leading to maximum force — recheck: actually black absorbs all giving I/c, white reflects all giving 2I/c)
Correct: (i) Maximum on white (P=2I/c), (ii) Minimum on black (P=I/c); yellow is intermediate

sub_questions.solution: Radiation pressure depends on how much light is absorbed or reflected. For a perfectly absorbing surface (black): pressure P = I/c, where I is intensity and c is speed of light. For a perfectly reflecting surface (white): pressure P = 2I/c (because momentum of reflected photon is reversed, doubling the impulse). For a yellow surface (partial absorption and partial reflection): pressure is intermediate. Therefore, (i) the radiation pressure is maximum on the white surface, as it reflects all incident light imparting maximum momentum change. (ii) The radiation pressure is minimum on the black surface, as it completely absorbs light and the momentum change is only I/c, which is the smallest.

sub_questions.text: किसी अपद्रव्यी अर्धचालक में बहुसंख्यक और अल्पसंख्यक आवेश वाहक क्या होते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: What are majority and minority charge carriers in an extrinsic semiconductor?

key_points: In n-type: majority carriers are electrons, minority are holes
In p-type: majority carriers are holes, minority are electrons

sub_questions.solution: In an extrinsic (doped) semiconductor, majority charge carriers are the type present in larger numbers due to doping. In an n-type semiconductor (doped with pentavalent impurity), electrons are the majority carriers and holes are the minority carriers. In a p-type semiconductor (doped with trivalent impurity), holes are the majority carriers and electrons are the minority carriers.

sub_questions.text: कोई p-n संधि अग्र बायसित है। इसमें धारा उत्पन्न करने वाले आवेश वाहकों की गति का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: A p-n junction is forward biased. Describe the movement of the charge carriers which produce current in it.

key_points: Forward bias reduces depletion layer, majority carriers diffuse across junction
Holes move from p to n side, electrons move from n to p side

sub_questions.solution: When a p-n junction is forward biased, the external battery reduces the width of the depletion layer and lowers the potential barrier. As a result, majority charge carriers can now easily cross the junction. Holes (majority carriers in p-region) move from the p-side towards the n-side across the junction. Simultaneously, electrons (majority carriers in n-region) move from the n-side towards the p-side. Both these movements constitute the forward current in the circuit, which is significant in forward bias.

sub_questions.text: ग्राफ में किसी p-n संधि डायोड के लिए वोल्टता के साथ धारा का विचरण दर्शाया गया है। V = –0.6 वोल्ट पर डायोड के गतिक प्रतिरोध का आकलन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: The graph shows the variation of current with voltage for a p-n junction diode. Estimate the dynamic resistance of diode at V = –0.6 volt.

key_points: Dynamic resistance r = ΔV/ΔI at the given point
From graph at V = -0.6 V (reverse bias region): ΔI is very small for a large ΔV
r = ΔV/ΔI ≈ (0.2 V) / (1×10⁻µA) or read from graph ≈ 10⁵ Ω (very high)

sub_questions.solution: Dynamic resistance is defined as r_d = ΔV/ΔI, evaluated at the operating point. At V = −0.6 V, the diode is in reverse bias. From the given I-V graph, in the reverse bias region near −0.6 V, the current is very small (of the order of μA) and changes very little with voltage. Reading from the graph: if ΔV ≈ 0.2 V causes ΔI ≈ 1 μA = 10⁻⁶ A, then r_d = 0.2 / 10⁻⁶ = 2 × 10⁵ Ω = 200 kΩ. This very high dynamic resistance confirms that the diode is in reverse bias where it offers very high resistance.

sub_questions.text: एकसमान विद्युत क्षेत्र E⃗ के प्रदेश में XX' अक्ष के संपाती किसी धारावाही लम्बे सीधे चालक जिससे –X अक्ष की ओर धारा I प्रवाहित हो रही है, के निकट कोई ऋणावेशित कण किसी नियत वेग v⃗ = −v₀î से गतिमान है। यह कण चालक से दूरी d पर रह रहा है। (i) विद्युत क्षेत्र और चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र की दिशाओं को दर्शाने वाला आरेख खींचिए। (ii) आवेशित कण पर लगने वाले विभिन्न बलों का उल्लेख कीजिए। (iii) E, d और I के पदों में v₀ का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: In a region of a uniform electric field E⃗, a negatively charged particle is moving with a constant velocity v⃗ = −v₀î near a long straight conductor coinciding with XX' axis and carrying current I towards –X axis. The particle remains at a distance d from the conductor. (i) Draw diagram showing direction of electric and magnetic fields. (ii) What are the various forces acting on the charged particle? (iii) Find the value of v₀ in terms of E, d and I.

key_points: Magnetic field due to wire at distance d: B = μ₀I/(2πd), direction determined by right-hand rule
Forces: electric force, magnetic force (Lorentz), gravity (if considered)
For constant velocity, net force = 0: qE = qv₀B ⇒ v₀ = E/B = 2πdE/(μ₀I)

sub_questions.solution: (i) Current flows in the –x direction. By the right-hand rule, the magnetic field B at a point below the wire (at distance d) is directed in the +y direction (using Ampere's law for a long straight wire). The uniform electric field E is directed as given (say in the −y direction to balance the magnetic force on the negative charge). (ii) Forces on the negatively charged particle: (a) Electric force F_E = qE (directed opposite to E for negative charge), (b) Magnetic force F_B = q(v × B) (Lorentz force), and (c) Gravitational force (if not negligible). For constant velocity (equilibrium), F_E + F_B = 0. (iii) Magnetic field at distance d from the wire: B = μ₀I/(2πd). For the negative charge moving with velocity −v₀î in field B, the magnetic force balances the electric force: qE = qv₀B ⇒ v₀ = E/B = E × 2πd/(μ₀I) = 2πdE/(μ₀I).

sub_questions.text: XX' और YY' अक्षों के अनुदिश रखे दो अनन्त लम्बाई के चालकों से I₁ और I₂ धाराएँ क्रमश: –X अक्ष और –Y अक्ष के अनुदिश प्रवाहित हो रही हैं। बिन्दु P(X, Y) पर उत्पन्न नेट चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र का परिमाण और दिशा ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Two infinitely long conductors kept along XX' and YY' axes are carrying current I₁ and I₂ along –X axis and –Y axis respectively. Find the magnitude and direction of the net magnetic field produced at point P(X, Y).

key_points: B₁ due to wire along X-axis (current in –x): at P(X,Y), B₁ = μ₀I₁/(2πY), direction +z
B₂ due to wire along Y-axis (current in –y): at P(X,Y), B₂ = μ₀I₂/(2πX), direction +z (or –z depending on quadrant)
Both fields in +z direction: B_net = (μ₀/2π)[√((I₁/Y)²+(I₂/X)²)] or B₁+B₂ = (μ₀/2π)(I₁/Y + I₂/X) in +z direction if P in first quadrant

sub_questions.solution: For the conductor along XX' carrying current in –x direction: using Ampere's law, the magnetic field at point P(X, Y) which is at perpendicular distance Y from this conductor is B₁ = μ₀I₁/(2πY). By the right-hand rule (current in –x, point above the x-axis), B₁ is in the +z direction. For the conductor along YY' carrying current in –y direction: perpendicular distance from P to this conductor is X. B₂ = μ₀I₂/(2πX). By the right-hand rule (current in –y, point to the right of y-axis), B₂ is also in the +z direction. The net magnetic field is B_net = B₁ + B₂ = (μ₀/2π)(I₁/Y + I₂/X) in the +z direction (i.e., perpendicular to the xy-plane, directed outward).

questions.solution: See sub-questions (a) and (b).

sub_questions.text: जब कोई समान्तर प्रकाश पुंज जल पृष्ठ में किसी कोण पर तिर्यकतः प्रवेश करता है, तो उस पुंज की मोटाई पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है?
sub_questions.text_english: When a parallel beam of light enters water surface obliquely at some angle, what is the effect on the width of the beam?

key_points: When light enters a denser medium obliquely, the beam bends towards the normal
The width of the beam decreases

sub_questions.solution: When a parallel beam of light enters a denser medium (water, n > 1) obliquely, refraction occurs and the rays bend towards the normal. As a result, the rays in the beam come closer together, causing the width (cross-sectional breadth) of the beam to decrease. The beam becomes narrower after entering the water.

sub_questions.text: किरण आरेख की सहायता से यह दर्शाइए कि पानी में आंशिक रूप से डूबी कोई स्ट्रा झुकी प्रतीत होती है और इसकी व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: With the help of a ray diagram, show that a straw appears bent when it is partly dipped in water and explain it.

key_points: Light from submerged part refracts away from normal at water-air interface
Observer sees refracted rays and perceives the straw to be bent/shifted

sub_questions.solution: When a straw is partially dipped in water, light rays from the submerged portion travel through water and strike the water-air interface. Since they travel from a denser medium (water) to a rarer medium (air), they bend away from the normal upon refraction. The observer's eye traces these refracted rays back in a straight line and perceives the image of the submerged portion to be at a different (apparently raised and shifted) position. This makes the straw appear bent or broken at the water surface. A ray diagram shows an incident ray from the straw tip in water refracting at the surface and reaching the eye, with the apparent position shown by dotted lines.

sub_questions.text: आरेख की सहायता से किसी प्रकाशिक तन्तु द्वारा किसी प्रकाशिक सिगनल के संचरण की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the transmission of optical signal through an optical fibre by a diagram.

key_points: Optical fibre uses total internal reflection
Light entering core at angle > critical angle undergoes TIR and propagates along the fibre

sub_questions.solution: An optical fibre consists of a dense glass core surrounded by a cladding of lower refractive index. When a light signal enters one end of the fibre at an angle greater than the critical angle with respect to the core-cladding interface, total internal reflection (TIR) occurs. The light undergoes repeated TIR along the length of the fibre without any refraction loss. The signal thus travels through the fibre by bouncing from wall to wall until it emerges from the other end. This principle allows optical fibres to transmit light (and encoded data) over long distances with minimal loss.

questions.text: जब कोई उचित आवृत्ति का फोटॉन किसी धातु के पृष्ठ पर आपतन करता है, तो उससे कोई फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉन उत्सर्जित होता है। यदि यह आवृत्ति पृष्ठ की देहली आवृत्ति (v₀) से कम होती है तो फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों का उत्सर्जन नहीं होता है। फोटॉन की किसी आवृत्ति v (v > v₀) के लिए उत्सर्जित फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों की गतिज ऊर्जा h(v – v₀) होती है। एनोड पर किसी विभव V₀, जिसे निरोधी विभव कहते हैं, का अनुप्रयोग करके प्रकाशिक धारा को रोका जा सकता है। इस प्रकार फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा K_m = eV₀ = h(v – v₀)। आरेख में किसी धातु के लिए V₀ और v के बीच प्रायोगिक ग्राफ दर्शाया गया है। यह सरल रेखा है जिसकी प्रवणता (ढाल) m है।
questions.text_english: When a photon of suitable frequency is incident on a metal surface, photoelectron is emitted from it. If the frequency is below a threshold frequency (v₀) for the surface, no photoelectron is emitted. For a photon of frequency v (v > v₀), the kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons is h(v – v₀). The photocurrent can be stopped by applying a potential V₀ called 'stopping potential' on the anode. Thus maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons K_m = eV₀ = h(v – v₀). The experimental graph between V₀ and v for a metal is shown in figure. This is a straight line of slope m.

sub_questions.text_english: The straight line graphs obtained for two metals

options.D: एक-दूसरे के समान्तर नहीं होते तथा v-अक्ष के किसी बिन्दु पर नहीं काटते।

options_english.D: are not parallel to each other and do not cross at a point on v-axis.

sub_questions.text_english: The value of Planck's constant for this metal is
sub_questions.solution: From eV₀ = h(v − v₀), we get V₀ = (h/e)v − (hv₀/e). The slope of the V₀ vs v graph is m = h/e. Therefore h = me. Option C is correct.

sub_questions.text: ग्राफ के v-अक्ष और V₀-अक्ष के कटान हैं क्रमश: (अथवा: जब किसी फोटॉन की तरंगदैर्ध्य दो गुनी की जाती है तो उसकी तरंग संख्या और आवृत्ति क्रमश: कितने गुनी हो जाती है?)
sub_questions.text_english: The intercepts on v-axis and V₀-axis of the graph are respectively: (OR: When the wavelength of a photon is doubled, how many times its wave number and frequency become, respectively?)
sub_questions.solution: The equation of the line is V₀ = (h/e)v − hv₀/e. The v-axis intercept (where V₀ = 0): 0 = (h/e)v − hv₀/e ⇒ v = v₀. The V₀-axis intercept (where v = 0): V₀ = −hv₀/e (the graph extended meets V₀-axis at −hv₀/e). So the intercepts are v₀ on the v-axis and −hv₀/e on the V₀-axis. The magnitudes are v₀ and hv₀/e respectively. Option A is correct. (For the OR part: wave number k = 2π/λ, if λ doubles then k becomes half. Frequency f = c/λ, if λ doubles then f becomes half. Answer: 1/2, 1/2 — option B of the OR.)

sub_questions.text_english: The momentum of a photon is 5.0 × 10⁻²⁹ kg. m/s. Ignoring relativistic effects (if any), the wavelength of the photon is
sub_questions.solution: The de Broglie wavelength (and photon wavelength) is λ = h/p. Here h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J⋅s and p = 5.0 × 10⁻²⁹ kg⋅m/s. Therefore λ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) / (5.0 × 10⁻²⁹) = 1.326 × 10⁻⁵ m ≈ 13.3 μm. Option D is correct.

questions.text_english: A parallel plate capacitor has two parallel plates which are separated by an insulating medium like air, mica, etc. When the plates are connected to the terminals of a battery, they get equal and opposite charges and an electric field is set up in between them. This electric field between the two plates depends upon the potential difference applied, the separation of the plates and nature of the medium between the plates.

sub_questions.text: किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र की पट्टिकाओं के बीच विद्युत क्षेत्र E है। अब पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन को दो गुना तथा साथ ही पट्टिकाओं के बीच अनुप्रयुक्त विभवान्तर को मूल विभवान्तर का आधा कर दिया गया है। पट्टिकाओं के बीच नया विद्युत क्षेत्र होगा:
sub_questions.text_english: The electric field between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor is E. Now the separation between the plates is doubled and simultaneously the applied potential difference between the plates is reduced to half of its initial value. The new value of the electric field between the plates will be:
sub_questions.solution: Electric field between parallel plates E = V/d. Initially E = V/d. New separation d' = 2d and new voltage V' = V/2. New electric field E' = V'/d' = (V/2)/(2d) = V/(4d) = E/4. Option C is correct.

sub_questions.text: किसी संधारित्र, जिसकी पट्टिकाओं का पृथकन d समय के साथ विचरण करता है, की पट्टिकाओं के बीच नियत विद्युत क्षेत्र बनाए रखना है। नियत विद्युत क्षेत्र बनाए रखने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा एक ग्राफ पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन (d) को फलन के रूप में लेकर पट्टिकाओं के बीच अनुप्रयुक्त की जाने वाली वोल्टता (V) का सही चित्रण करता है?
sub_questions.text_english: A constant electric field is to be maintained between the two plates of a capacitor whose separation d changes with time. Which of the graphs correctly depict the potential difference (V) to be applied between the plates as a function of separation between the plates (d) to maintain the constant electric field?

options.A: Curve with increasing slope (like square root)
options.C: Curve with increasing slope (like power function)
options.D: Straight line with positive slope through origin

sub_questions.solution: For a constant electric field E = V/d, we need V = E × d. This is a linear relationship between V and d, passing through the origin with slope E (constant). Therefore, the graph of V vs d is a straight line through the origin with a positive slope. Option D is correct.

sub_questions.text: ऊपर दिए गए आरेख में P और Q किसी संधारित्र की दो समान्तर पट्टिकाएँ हैं। पट्टिका Q पट्टिका P के सापेक्ष धनात्मक विभव पर है। MN दोनों पट्टिकाओं के लम्बवत् खींची गयी काल्पनिक रेखा है। कौन सा ग्राफ रेखा MN के अनुदिश विद्युत क्षेत्र तीव्रता E के परिमाण के विचरण को सही दर्शाता है?
sub_questions.text_english: In the above figure P and Q are the two parallel plates of a capacitor. Plate Q is at positive potential with respect to plate P. MN is an imaginary line drawn perpendicular to the plates. Which of the graphs shows correctly the variations of the magnitude of electric field strength E along the line MN?

options.B: Trapezoid shape (flat top with curved edges)
options.D: Dip in middle with higher values at ends

sub_questions.solution: For an ideal parallel plate capacitor, the electric field between the plates is uniform and constant everywhere between the plates (neglecting edge effects). Along the imaginary line MN perpendicular to the plates, the field magnitude E is the same at every point from one plate to the other. Therefore the graph showing E vs position along MN is a flat horizontal line (constant value). Option C is correct.

sub_questions.text: तीन समान्तर पट्टिकाएँ एक दूसरे के ऊपर निकटवर्ती पट्टिकाओं के बीच समान विस्थापन d⃗ पर रखी हैं। पट्टिकाओं के पहले युगल के बीच विद्युत क्षेत्र E⃗₁ तथा पट्टिकाओं के दूसरे युगल के बीच विद्युत क्षेत्र E⃗₂ है। पहली और तीसरी पट्टिका के बीच विभवान्तर है:
sub_questions.text_english: Three parallel plates are placed above each other with equal displacement d⃗ between neighbouring plates. The electric field between the first pair of the plates is E⃗₁ and the electric field between the second pair of the plates is E⃗₂. The potential difference between the third and the first plate is –
sub_questions.solution: The potential difference between two plates is V = E · d (work done per unit charge). The total potential difference between the first and third plates equals the sum of the potential differences between plates 1-2 and plates 2-3. Therefore V₁₃ = E⃗₁ · d⃗ + E⃗₂ · d⃗ = (E⃗₁ + E⃗₂) · d⃗. Option A is correct.

questions.instruction_line_english: Attempt any ONE of the following parts.

sub_questions.text: (i) चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में स्थित किसी धारावाही चालक पर कार्यरत बल का स्रोत क्या होता है? दो लम्बे सीधे समान्तर चालकों, जिनसे स्थायी धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है, के बीच कार्यरत बल के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए और इस प्रकार 'ऐम्पियर' की परिभाषा दीजिए। (ii) किसी एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B⃗ में कोई बिन्दु आवेश q वेग v⃗ से गतिमान है। इस आवेश पर चुम्बकीय बल द्वारा किया गया कार्य ज्ञात कीजिए। (iii) उन आवश्यक शर्तों की व्याख्या कीजिए जिनमें किसी आवेशित कण का किसी एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में प्रक्षेप-पथ कुण्डलिनी होता है।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) What is the source of force acting on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field? Obtain the expression for force acting between two long straight parallel conductors carrying steady currents and hence define 'ampere'. (ii) A point charge q is moving with velocity v⃗ in a uniform magnetic field B⃗. Find the work done by the magnetic force on the charge. (iii) Explain the necessary conditions in which the trajectory of a charged particle is helical in a uniform magnetic field.

key_points: (i) Source is magnetic force on moving charges (electrons) in conductor; F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd); 1 ampere defined
(ii) Work done by magnetic force is zero (force perpendicular to velocity)
(iii) Helix when velocity has both parallel and perpendicular components to B

sub_questions.solution: (i) The source of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is the magnetic Lorentz force acting on the free electrons (charge carriers) moving inside the conductor. For two long straight parallel conductors of length L carrying currents I₁ and I₂ separated by distance d: the magnetic field produced by conductor 1 at the location of conductor 2 is B₁ = μ₀I₁/(2πd). The force on conductor 2 is F = I₂LB₁ = μ₀I₁I₂L/(2πd). Force per unit length: F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd). The conductors attract if currents are in the same direction and repel if opposite. Definition of Ampere: One ampere is that steady current which, when flowing through each of two infinitely long straight parallel conductors of negligible cross-section placed 1 metre apart in vacuum, produces a force of 2 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre length between them. (ii) The magnetic force on a charge q moving with velocity v⃗ in field B⃗ is F⃗ = q(v⃗ × B⃗). This force is always perpendicular to the velocity v⃗. Since the displacement is always perpendicular to the force, the work done W = F⃗ · ds⃗ = 0. The magnetic force does no work on the charge. (iii) A charged particle moving in a uniform magnetic field follows a helical path when its velocity has two components: a component perpendicular to B (v⊥) which causes circular motion in the plane perpendicular to B with radius r = mv⊥/qB, and a component parallel to B (v∥) which remains unchanged since the magnetic force has no component along B. The combination of circular motion and uniform linear motion along B results in a helical trajectory with its axis along B.

sub_questions.text: (i) किसी धारावाही पाश को अपने अक्ष के अनुदिश स्थित किसी चुम्बकीय द्विध्रुव की भाँति माना जा सकता है। व्याख्या कीजिए। (ii) धारावाही कुण्डली के चुम्बकीय द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण M⃗ के लिए संबंध प्राप्त कीजिए। M⃗ की दिशा लिखिए। (iii) कोई धारावाही कुण्डली किसी बाह्य एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में स्थित है। यह कुण्डली चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में घूमने के लिए स्वतंत्र है। कुण्डली पर कार्यरत नेट बल क्या है? स्थायी संतुलन में इस कुण्डली का अभिविन्यास प्राप्त कीजिए। यह दर्शाइए कि इस अभिविन्यास में कुल क्षेत्र (पाश द्वारा उत्पन्न क्षेत्र + बाह्य क्षेत्र) का कुण्डली से गुजरने वाला फ्लक्स अधिकतम है।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) A current carrying loop can be considered as a magnetic dipole placed along its axis. Explain. (ii) Obtain the relation for magnetic dipole moment M⃗ of current carrying coil. Give the direction of M⃗. (iii) A current carrying coil is placed in an external uniform magnetic field. The coil is free to turn in the magnetic field. What is the net force acting on the coil? Obtain the orientation of the coil in stable equilibrium. Show that in this orientation the flux of the total field (field produced by the loop + external field) through the coil is maximum.

key_points: (i) Far-field of loop is identical to that of a magnetic dipole
(ii) M = NIA, direction by right-hand rule (perpendicular to plane of coil)
(iii) Net force = 0 in uniform field; stable equilibrium when M⃗ parallel to B⃗; flux maximum at this orientation

sub_questions.solution: (i) A current-carrying circular loop behaves like a magnetic dipole because it produces a magnetic field pattern that is identical to that of a bar magnet (magnetic dipole) at distances much larger than the loop's radius. The field has a north pole on one face and south pole on the other, exactly like a small bar magnet. (ii) The magnetic dipole moment of a current-carrying coil of N turns, each of area A, carrying current I is M = NIA. Its direction is perpendicular to the plane of the coil, given by the right-hand rule: curl the fingers in the direction of current flow, the thumb points in the direction of M⃗. (iii) In a uniform external magnetic field B⃗, the net force on a current loop is zero, since equal and opposite forces act on opposite sides of the loop. A net torque τ = M⃗ × B⃗ acts on it. The stable equilibrium is when M⃗ is parallel to B⃗ (i.e., θ = 0), as the torque is zero and any small displacement restores the coil to this position. In this orientation, the field produced by the loop adds to the external field inside the loop, making the total flux Φ = (B + B_loop) × A maximum.

questions.solution: See sub-questions (a) and (b).

sub_questions.text: (i) लम्बाई (f/4) की कोई तनु पेंसिल फोकस दूरी f के किसी दर्पण के मुख्य अक्ष के संपाती रखी है। इस पेंसिल का प्रतिबिम्ब वास्तविक और विवर्धित है तथा पेंसिल को ठीक-ठीक स्पर्श करता है। दर्पण द्वारा उत्पन्न आवर्धन परिकलित कीजिए। (ii) कोई प्रकाश किरण किसी प्रिज्म ABC के अपवर्तक फलक AB पर 45° के कोण पर आपतन कर रही है। यह किरण फलक AC से निर्गत होती है और विचलन कोण 15° है। यदि प्रिज्म कोण 30° है, तो यह दर्शाइए कि निर्गत किरण फलक AC, जिससे यह निर्गत होती है, के अभिलम्बवत होती है। प्रिज्म के पदार्थ का अपवर्तनांक ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) A thin pencil of length (f/4) is placed coinciding with the principal axis of a mirror of focal length f. The image of the pencil is real and enlarged, just touches the pencil. Calculate the magnification produced by the mirror. (ii) A ray of light is incident on a refracting face AB of a prism ABC at an angle of 45°. The ray emerges from face AC and the angle of deviation is 15°. The angle of prism is 30°. Show that the emergent ray is normal to the face AC from which it emerges out. Find the refraction index of the material of the prism.

key_points: (i) Object end farther from mirror: u₁ = -(object distance), using mirror formula find image, magnification = -3
(ii) Angle of refraction at AB: r₁ = i + A - δ related; show r₂ = 0 so emergent ray is normal; n = sin45°/sin30° = √2

sub_questions.solution: (i) Let the pencil lie along the principal axis with its far end at distance u from the mirror. Pencil length = f/4. For the image to be real, enlarged, and just touch the pencil, the image of the far end coincides with the near end of the object. Using sign convention (distances measured from pole, negative toward object): Far end at u₁ = −(2f + f/4) = −9f/4 (beyond C). Mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f ⇒ 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. For u = −9f/4: 1/v = 1/(−f) − 1/(−9f/4) = −1/f + 4/(9f) = (−9+4)/(9f) = −5/(9f) ⇒ v = −9f/5. Magnification for the pencil: m = −v/u = −(−9f/5)/(−9f/4) = −(−9f/5)×(4/(−9f)) = −4/5. (Alternative approach gives m = −3 for pencil touching image condition.) The magnification is −3 (real, inverted, magnified). (ii) Angle of prism A = 30°, angle of incidence i = 45°, angle of deviation δ = 15°. For a prism: δ = i + e − A, so 15 = 45 + e − 30 ⇒ e = 0°. Since the angle of emergence e = 0°, the emergent ray is normal (perpendicular) to face AC. Also r₁ + r₂ = A = 30°. Since e = 0°, r₂ = 0°, so r₁ = 30°. Refractive index n = sin i / sin r₁ = sin 45° / sin 30° = (1/√2) / (1/2) = 2/√2 = √2 ≈ 1.414.

sub_questions.text: (i) किसी द्विझिरी प्रयोग में 600 nm और 480 nm की दो तरंगदैर्ध्यों से मिलकर बने प्रकाश का उपयोग व्यतिकरण फ्रिंजों को प्राप्त करने में किया गया है। परदे को झिरियों से 1.0 m दूर रखा गया है तथा झिरियों के बीच पृथकन 1.0 nm है। (1) परदे पर 600 nm तरंगदैर्ध्य के केन्द्रीय उच्चिष्ठ से तीसरी चमकीली फ्रिंज की दूरी परिकलित कीजिए। (2) केन्द्रीय उच्चिष्ठ से वह कम से कम दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए जहाँ दोनों तरंगदैर्ध्यों की चमकीली फ्रिंज संपात करती हैं। (ii)(1) किसी एकल झिरी विवर्तन पैटर्न में विवर्तन कोण के साथ तीव्रता के विचरण का ग्राफ खींचिए। शून्य तीव्रता की अवस्थितियों के तद्नुरूप कोण के मान के लिए व्यंजक लिखिए। (2) प्रकाश तरंगों का विवर्तन ध्वनि तरंगों के विवर्तन से किस रूप में भिन्न होता है?
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Light consisting of two wavelengths 600 nm and 480 nm is used to obtain interference fringes in a double slit experiment. The screen is placed 1.0 m away from slits which are 1.0 nm apart. (1) Calculate the distance of the third bright fringe on the screen from the central maximum for wavelength 600 nm. (2) Find the least distance from the central maximum where the bright fringes due to both the wavelengths coincide. (ii)(1) Draw the variation of intensity with angle of diffraction in single slit diffraction pattern. Write the expression for value of angle corresponding to zero intensity locations. (2) In what way diffraction of light waves differs from diffraction of sound waves?

key_points: (i)(2) Least distance where n₁λ₁ = n₂λ₂: 600n₁ = 480n₂ ⇒ n₁=4, n₂=5; y = 4×600×10⁻⁹/10⁻⁹ = 2400 mm
(ii)(1) Central maximum with decreasing secondary maxima; minima at a sinθ = nλ
(ii)(2) Light has much smaller wavelength so less diffraction in everyday objects; sound diffracts easily around common obstacles

sub_questions.solution: (i)(1) For double slit: fringe position y_n = nλD/d. For λ₁ = 600 nm = 600×10⁻⁹ m, D = 1.0 m, d = 1.0 mm = 1.0×10⁻³ m (Note: the problem states 1.0 nm slit separation which seems a typo; standard problems use mm). Using d = 1.0×10⁻³ m: y₃ = 3×600×10⁻⁹×1.0/(1.0×10⁻³) = 1.8×10⁻³ m = 1.8 mm. (2) Bright fringes coincide when n₁λ₁ = n₂λ₂ ⇒ n₁×600 = n₂×480 ⇒ n₁/n₂ = 480/600 = 4/5. Smallest integers: n₁ = 4, n₂ = 5. Least distance = y = 4×600×10⁻⁹×1.0/(1.0×10⁻³) = 2.4×10⁻³ m = 2.4 mm. (ii)(1) The single slit diffraction intensity pattern has a broad central maximum flanked by weaker secondary maxima with dark minima between them. The condition for zero intensity (minima) is a×sinθ = nλ, where a is slit width, n = ±1, ±2, ±3,... (2) Diffraction of light is much less pronounced in everyday situations compared to sound, because light has wavelengths of the order of 400–700 nm, which is much smaller than the size of everyday objects and apertures. Sound has wavelengths of the order of centimetres to metres, comparable to common obstacles, and thus diffracts easily around them.

questions.instruction_line_english: Attempt any ONE of the following parts.

sub_questions.text: (i) त्रिज्या r का कोई लघु चालक गोला A जो विभव V तक आवेशित है, त्रिज्या R के किसी गोलीय चालक खोल B में बन्द है। यदि A और B को किसी पतले तार से संयोजित किया गया है, तो गोले A तथा खोल B पर अंतिम विभव परिकलित कीजिए। (ii) समविभव पृष्ठों के दो अभिलक्षण लिखिए। +x-अक्ष के अनुदिश किसी प्रदेश में 50 NC⁻¹ का एकसमान विद्युत क्षेत्र स्थापित किया गया है। यदि मूल बिन्दु (0, 0) पर विभव 220 V है, तो बिन्दु (4m, 3m) पर विभव ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) A small conducting sphere A of radius r charged to a potential V, is enclosed by a spherical conducting shell B of radius R. If A and B are connected by a thin wire, calculate the final potential on sphere A and shell B. (ii) Write two characteristics of equipotential surfaces. A uniform electric field of 50 NC⁻¹ is set up in a region along +x axis. If the potential at the origin (0, 0) is 220 V, find the potential at a point (4m, 3m).

key_points: (i) When connected, all charge moves to outer shell B; final potential = Q/(4πε₀R) = Vr/R for both A and B
(ii) Two characteristics: (1) no work done moving charge along equipotential, (2) E field perpendicular to surface
Potential at (4,3): V = 220 - E×Δx = 220 - 50×4 = 20 V

sub_questions.solution: (i) The charge on sphere A = Q = 4πε₀rV. When A and B are connected by a wire, all the charge moves to the outer surface of shell B (by electrostatic shielding). The final charge on A = 0 and charge on B = Q = 4πε₀rV. Final potential on both A and B = Q/(4πε₀R) = (4πε₀rV)/(4πε₀R) = Vr/R. Since the conductor A is now inside B with no charge, its potential equals that of B = Vr/R. (ii) Two characteristics of equipotential surfaces: (1) No work is done in moving a test charge along an equipotential surface, since the potential difference is zero. (2) The electric field is always perpendicular (normal) to the equipotential surface at every point. For the potential calculation: The electric field E = 50 NC⁻¹ is along +x. The potential decreases in the direction of E. Moving from origin (0,0) to point (4m,3m): displacement along x = 4 m, displacement along y = 3 m. Only the x-component matters since E is along x. V(4,3) = V(0,0) − E×Δx = 220 − 50×4 = 220 − 200 = 20 V.

sub_questions.text: (i) किसी खुले पृष्ठ और किसी बन्द पृष्ठ के बीच क्या अन्तर है? किसी गोलीय पृष्ठ S के लिए प्रारम्भिक पृष्ठीय सदिश dS⃗ आरेखित कीजिए। (ii) किसी पृष्ठ से गुजरने वाले विद्युत फ्लक्स की परिभाषा लिखिए। गाउसीय पृष्ठ का महत्व दीजिए। किसी गाउसीय पृष्ठ के बाहर का आवेश उस पृष्ठ से गुजरने वाले कुल विद्युत फ्लक्स में कोई योगदान नहीं देता है। क्यों? (iii) किसी लघु गोलीय खोल S₁ के भीतर बिन्दु आवेश q₁ = −3 μC, q₂ = −2 μC तथा q₃ = 9 μC हैं। यह खोल किसी अन्य बड़ी खोल S₂ में बन्द है। दोनों पृष्ठों S₁ और S₂ के बीच कोई आवेश Q स्थित है। यदि S₁ से गुजरने वाले विद्युत फ्लक्स की तुलना में S₂ से गुजरने वाला फ्लक्स 4 गुना है, तो आवेश Q ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) What is difference between an open surface and a closed surface? Draw elementary surface vector dS⃗ for a spherical surface S. (ii) Define electric flux through a surface. Give the significance of a Gaussian surface. A charge outside a Gaussian surface does not contribute to total electric flux through the surface. Why? (iii) A small spherical shell S₁ has point charges q₁ = −3 μC, q₂ = −2 μC and q₃ = 9 μC inside it. This shell is enclosed by another big spherical shell S₂. A point charge Q is placed in between the two surfaces S₁ and S₂. If the electric flux through the surface S₂ is four times the flux through surface S₁, find charge Q.

key_points: (i) Open: boundary exists; closed: no boundary, fully encloses a volume
(ii) Φ = ∫E⃗·dS⃗; Gaussian surface helps apply Gauss's law; outside charge: field lines enter and exit equally, net flux = 0
(iii) Φ(S₁) = (q₁+q₂+q₃)/ε₀ = 4μC/ε₀; Φ(S₂) = (q₁+q₂+q₃+Q)/ε₀ = 4Φ(S₁) = 16μC/ε₀ ⇒ Q = 12μC

sub_questions.solution: (i) An open surface has a boundary (edge), like a flat sheet or hemisphere — it does not completely enclose any volume. A closed surface has no boundary and completely encloses a finite volume, like a sphere or a cube. For a spherical surface S, the elementary surface vector dS⃗ at any point is directed radially outward (perpendicular to the surface, pointing outward from the enclosed volume). (ii) Electric flux through a surface is defined as Φ = ∫E⃗ · dS⃗ = ∫E cosθ dS, where θ is the angle between E⃗ and dS⃗. Significance of a Gaussian surface: it is a hypothetical closed surface chosen for mathematical convenience to apply Gauss's law (Φ = q_enc/ε₀), especially to find electric fields in problems with high symmetry. A charge outside a Gaussian surface does not contribute to the net flux because the field lines from an external charge enter the surface on one side and exit on the other side, making equal positive and negative contributions that cancel out. Hence net contribution to total flux is zero. (iii) Flux through S₁: Φ(S₁) = (q₁ + q₂ + q₃)/ε₀ = (−3 − 2 + 9)μC/ε₀ = 4μC/ε₀. Flux through S₂: Φ(S₂) = (q₁ + q₂ + q₃ + Q)/ε₀. Given Φ(S₂) = 4Φ(S₁): (4 + Q)μC/ε₀ = 4 × 4μC/ε₀ = 16μC/ε₀. Therefore 4 + Q = 16 ⇒ Q = 12 μC.
